issues.description: Duplicate 'transcriber_error' literal in error-message tuple signals a spec without a single source of truth
issues.detail: The membership tuple lists 'transcriber_error' twice. This is the symptom of a missing ADT: the set of error message_types is the contract between ElevenLabs and this consumer, but it is expressed as an ad-hoc inline literal. Lift it to a named frozenset/Enum so the contract is stateable, testable, and de-duplicated.

issues.description: push_error contract is overloaded with formatting concerns the caller should not own
issues.detail: Each branch now prefixes 'Error: ' before pushing, but the previous code distinguished 'Auth error:' and 'Quota exceeded:'. Collapsing into one generic prefix weakens the postcondition of push_error's observers (they can no longer distinguish error class without re-parsing). Either pass message_type as a structured field, or restore typed prefixes — do not silently weaken the postcondition.

issues.description: Removing the outer try/except changes _receive_messages's failure contract without updating the supertype expectation
issues.detail: _receive_messages is invoked by the websocket_service reconnect loop, whose precondition is that the coroutine raises on disconnect so the loop can reconnect. The old implementation caught and logged, then returned normally — which is exactly the infinite-loop bug. The fix is correct, but the contract ('this coroutine returns iff stream ended cleanly; raises on transport error') must be documented in the docstring so future subtypes do not re-introduce the swallow.

issues.description: Inner try/except Exception inside the async-for still risks masking transport errors
issues.detail: The remaining 'except Exception as e: logger.error(...)' inside the message loop will catch transport-level exceptions raised mid-iteration as well as JSON/handler errors. Narrow it to handler-domain exceptions, or re-raise after logging if the exception did not originate from _process_response, to preserve the 'raise on disconnect' contract that this PR is trying to establish.

issues.description: Renaming _process_messages to _receive_messages erases a useful abstraction layer
issues.detail: Previously _process_messages (per-message dispatch) and _receive_messages (lifecycle/recovery) were two distinct responsibilities at two boundaries. Collapsing them merges the dispatch ADT with the connection-lifecycle ADT. Keep both, and let _receive_messages delegate — that preserves substitutability if another transport (e.g., reconnect-with-resume) needs to wrap lifecycle without rewriting dispatch.

issues.description: Changelog file missing trailing newline — minor spec hygiene
issues.detail: changelog/3233.fixed.md lacks a terminating newline. Trivial, but the convention across the changelog directory is part of the implicit contract for the release-notes assembler. Add the newline.

review.summary: The PR fixes a real bug — the outer try/except in _receive_messages was swallowing disconnect exceptions and defeating the reconnect loop's precondition — and broadens the error message_type coverage. The contract-level concerns are: the set of error message_types should be a named ADT (the inline tuple already shows a duplicate 'transcriber_error'), the new collapsed 'Error:' prefix weakens push_error's observable postcondition relative to the old typed prefixes, and the new _receive_messages contract ('raises on transport error') should be documented so a future subtype does not re-introduce the swallow. Decision label: LSP-VIOLATION (weakened postcondition on push_error) plus SPEC-MISSING on the error-type set and the receive-loop contract.
